texts.preamble: State vs . Archana Gupta on 25 August, 2022 In The Court Of Ms. Alka Singh Metropolitan Magistrate-08 (South-West), Dwarka Courts, Delhi Dlsw020218152019 In The Matter Of : State Vs. Archana Gupta Fir No.384/2011 Ps : Uttam Nagar U/s 336/337 Ipc Date of Institution : 01.09.2012 Date of Judgment : 25.08.2022 Judgment
texts.facts: It has been alleged by the prosecution that the accused Archana Gupta, who was a contractor hired to supply Midday Meal to Sarvodya Kanya Vidyalaya situated at Mohan Garden, Uttam Nagar, supplied the cooked meal of Kadhi Chawal in the said school on 03.09.2011, wherein a dead lizard was found in one tiffin box of a student. Further, consequent to consuming of the said meal, various children complained of nausea and stomach pain and fell ill. 3. After conclusion of investigation, the present chargesheet was filed against the accused u/s 336/337 IPC. 4. On receipt of chargesheet, cognizance of offence was taken. State Vs. Archana Gupta FIR No.384/2011, PS Uttam Nagar, Page No. 2 of 17 Judgment dated 25.08.2022 Copy of the chargesheet alongwith all annexures were supplied to the accused in terms of Section 207 Cr.P.C. 5. After giving opportunity to state as well as accused for making submissions on charge, a charge for offence u/s 336/337 IPC was framed against the accused on 27.01.2015, to which she pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 6. Prosecution examined ten witnesses to prove its case. 7. As PW1, HC Ratan Lal was examined who stated that on 03.09.2011, one plastic tiffin box and one steel container both containing Kadhi Chawal sealed with the seal of VS was produced by SI Vijender and was deposited in the maalkhana vide mud number 4616 in the register no.19. The said entry was Ex. PW1/A (OSR). He further deposed that on 05.09.2011, at the request of the IO, he gave the case property to SI Vijender vide RC no.114/31 for sending it to FSL and its RC was again deposited with the malkhana. He was not cross- examined despite opportunity. 8. As PW2 Smt. Pushpa Bhai, Retd. Principal of Govt. Sr. Secondary School, Uttam Nagar, Delhi, who avowed that on 03.09.2011, he was posted as Principal of Sarvodya Kanya Vidyalaya School, Mohan Garden and mid-Day Meal was served to the students through Indcare Trust Green Avenue, 66 Shiv Vihar owned by Reeva Sood. She deposed that Kadhi Chawal was served to the children on that day and one of the students namely Neha Pandey of class 8 th C State Vs. Archana Gupta FIR No.384/2011, PS Uttam Nagar, Page No. 3 of 17 Judgment dated 25.08.2022 came to her and made a complaint that one lizard was found in the kadhi and she immediately stopped all the students State vs . Archana Gupta on 25 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171946125/ 2 from eating the meal. She further testified that she checked the Kadhi Chawla served to Neha and found one lizard in the Kadhi and immediately informed her seniors and the govt. officers in charge of the Midday Meal. It was also averred by her that few of the students who have taken the meal were feeling uneasiness and complained of nausea, headache and stomach pain. She further testified that she immediately informed the police and the police took the students who were facing some problems to DDU Hospital and she lodged her complaint Ex. PW2/A (with the police). She also stated that the police took into possession the tiffin of Kadhi chawal in which the lizard was found vide seizure memo Ex. PW2/B and that she also produced the container which was seized vide seizure memos Ex. PW2/C and PW2/D. The witness then correctly identified the case property i.e., one pullanda sealed with the seal of VS and one envelope sealed with the seal of FSL SSK Delhi which were both opened and the pullanda was found to contain one steel container with cover Ex. P-1 while the envelope contained a red plastic tiffin box which was Ex. P-2, which the witness identified as the tiffin box given to student Neha Pandey. In her cross-examination, she stated that she does not know the name of the NGO or the name of the in charge who used to supply the midday meal in the school. She further deposed that there was the committee to supply the mid-day meal in the school but she does not State Vs. Archana Gupta FIR No.384/2011, PS Uttam Nagar, Page No. 4 of 17 Judgment dated 25.08.2022 remember who was the head of the said committee and then affirmed the suggestion of the defence counsel that Principal is the head of the said committee. It was also stated that mid-day meal was used to be tested in the school first before giving it to the students and she also affirmed the fact that on the day of the incident also the food was tested in the same manner as it was used to. She asserted that neither she nor any of the teacher tested the food on the day of the incident. She also could not tell the name of the teacher who received the meal on the day of the incident. She also did not remember the time when the food was supplied and then volunteered to state that it was supplied half an hour before the recession i.e., 10:00 AM. She could not tell to how many children; the mid-day meal was distributed on the day of the incident. She stated that the food sample was taken by the police in her presence and though she herself did not make any call to the NGO which supplied the meal but one of the teachers did call the NGO, but she could not remember the name of the said teacher. She also asserted that she visited the DDU hospital later on and inquired the doctor who attended the ill students and was informed that the girl students had nausea. All the adverse suggestions of the defence counsel were denied. 9. As PW3 Sh. A.K. Kaushik, Executive from Shriram Institute for Industrial Research was examined, who deposed that on the day of the incident he went to the Sarvodya School for collecting the mid-day meal sample and upon reaching in the school, he found that Principal State Vs. Archana Gupta FIR No.384/2011, PS Uttam Nagar, Page No. 5 of 17 Judgment dated 25.08.2022 and police officials were present there and he was informed that after taking the mid-day meal the students have become ill. Thereafter, he collected the sample, the tiffin and the container in which the mid day meal was brought, they were taken into possession and were sealed. The sample was then deposited at Sriram Institute for testing. Upon a leading question asked by the Ld. APP for State he confirmed that the tiffin and the container were sealed with the seal of VS. State vs . Archana Gupta on 25 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171946125/ 3 In his cross-examination, he stated that he collected the samples in two bottles and that he was called by the principal of the school. All the adverse suggestion of Ld. Defence counsel were denied by the witness. 10. As PW4 Ms. Neha Pandey, was examined who stated that in the year 2011 she was studying in class 8th in Sarvodaya Kanya Vidayalaya, Mohan Garden and on the day of the incident at 10:30 AM, she with her friend Neha Singh went to take the mid-day meal provided by the school and when they opened their tiffin boxes in the classroom, one dead lizard was found in the Kadhi Chawal which was distributed on that day. She further deposed that after seeing this she took the food to the office of the principal and made a complaint and the principal took the meal in her custody. Thereafter, the police arrived and recorded her statement. In her cross-examination, she stated that she does not remember if any teacher was present at the place from where the meal was being State Vs. Archana Gupta FIR No.384/2011, PS Uttam Nagar, Page No. 6 of 17 Judgment dated 25.08.2022 distributed but the meal was being distributed by one aunty whose name she did not remember. She stated that she and her friend did not consume the meal on that day but she was unsure of the fact if other student of class 8th ate the meal or not. 11. As PW5 Smt. Riva Sood was examined, who was the managing the Trustee and Education Trust of Indi-care Trust. It was stated by her that in the month of October, 2010 an SPA regarding providing of mid-day meals in Sarvodaya Vidaylaya, Mohan Garden was executed vide resolution dated 11.08.2010 in favour of Archana Gupta, the accused (who was present in the court and was correctly identified). Copy of the SPA was mark X. She deposed that accused was working as a Project Coordinator in the Trust and she was in the charge of looking after the mid-day meal. She further deposed that on 03.09.2011, the mid-day meal was supplied in Sarvodaya Kanya Vidyalaya as well as to other schools in the same zone from the same kitchen of their trust which was looked after by the accused Archana and her team. She stated that she was informed that on that day a lizard was found in the mid-day meals supplied in Sarvodaya Kanya Vidayalaya. She asserted that accused was under duty to look after the meals while it was being cooked and when the same was transported in the school. In her cross-examination, she stated that she received a information regarding the abovesaid incident from some journalist and that there is an MOU between their trust and the govt. for supplying State Vs. Archana Gupta FIR No.384/2011, PS Uttam Nagar, Page No. 7 of 17 Judgment dated 25.08.2022 the mid-day meal to govt. schools. The photocopy of the said MOU dated 15.01.2010 was Ex. PW5/DA. She further asserted that the role of the NGO which prepared the mid-day meal and transported it to the concerned school, was under the supervision of accused. She affirmed the suggestion that she did not receive any information regarding the incident from the school authority and she herself went to DDU hospital where she was informed by the doctors that all the children were examined and sent back as everything was alright and no treatment was given to any child. 12. As PW6 Ms. Gomati was examined, who stated that she was working in the office of Indcare Trust company, Green Avenue Shiv Vihar and was assigned the job of distributing the salary. She State vs . Archana Gupta on 25 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171946125/ 4 stated that Ms. Reeva Sood was working as the director of the said trust and deposed that she came to know that a lizard has been found in the mid-day meal served in the school. She also avouched that the duty to serve the mid-day meal was assigned to accused Archana Gupta (present in the court and correctly identified) and that accused used to get the mid-day meal prepared in the kitchen on behalf of the trust. She also stated that she cannot say if the accused was negligent on her part and also, she does not know if the accused was authorized to serve the mid-day meal. Because the witness was not supporting her previous statement, Ld. APP for the State was allowed to cross-examine her wherein she affirmed the fact that accused was assigned to serve the mid-day meal State Vs. Archana Gupta FIR No.384/2011, PS Uttam Nagar, Page No. 8 of 17 Judgment dated 25.08.2022 in Sarvodaya Kanya Vidayalaya School. She denied the suggestion regarding the SPA executed in favour of accused by Ms. Reeva Sood and also the fact that the lizard was found in the meal due to the negligence of the accused. She was confronted with her statement Mark X1 wherein it was so recorded. She was not cross-examined by the defence counsel. 13. As PW7 Ct. Renu was examined, who deposed that on 20.09.2011, she was posted at PS Uttam Nagar as Constable and on that day accused Archana Gupta was arrested and her personal search was conducted by her at the instruction of SI Vijender (accused was also correctly identified by the witness). The arrest memo and personal search memo were Ex. PW7/A and PW7/B respectively. Nothing significant was asked to the witness in the cross-examination. Therefore, the same is not being reproduced here. 14. As PW8 Retd. SI Nawal Singh was examined, who was only a formal witness and was called upon to testify regarding the rukka received by him from Ct. Vikas on the basis of which the FIR was registered. The FIR was Ex. PW8/A (OSR) and the endorsement on the rukka was Ex. PW8/B. All the adverse suggestions of Ld. Defence counsel were denied by the witness. 15. As PW9 Retd. WSI Rajbala was examined, who deposed that on 03.09.2011, she received an information which was reduced into writing as DD no.22A and about 03:45 PM, she received an State Vs. Archana Gupta FIR No.384/2011, PS Uttam Nagar, Page No. 9 of 17 Judgment dated 25.08.2022 information vide DD no.27A both the DDs were Ex. PW9/A and PW9/B respectively. She denied all the adverse suggestions of Ld. Defence counsel. 16. As PW10 ASI Vikas was examined, who described the investigation carried out by SI Vijender as he also accompanied him while visiting the school, pursuant to receiving of DD no.22A, where the principal gave her complaint upon which the tehrir was prepared and was given to him for registration of FIR. In his cross-examination, he stated that when he reached to the hospital the girls were under treatment and therefore, their statement was not recorded by the IO. 17. Since the accused admitted the FSL result and the MLCs nos.17897/11, 17928/11, 17929/11, 17898/11, 17925/11 and 17899/11 in terms of Section 294 Cr.P.C. and hence, the formal proof of the abovesaid documents were dispensed with. The FSL result was Ex. C- 1 and the MLCs were Ex. C-2 to Ex. C-7. State vs . Archana Gupta on 25 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171946125/ 5 18. Since, no other witness was examined by prosecution, hence, the PE was closed and statement of accused was recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C. to allow him to explain the incriminating circumstances appearing in evidences against him wherein it was stated by accused she is innocent and claimed that though the meal was prepared under her supervision but she did not herself prepared the meal rather it was prepared by her team and the meal was packed by some other team. She further asserted that she is not personally State Vs. Archana Gupta FIR No.384/2011, PS Uttam Nagar, Page No. 10 of 17 Judgment dated 25.08.2022 liable for any of the mis-happenings and she was not negligent in her duties. 19. Since the accused chose not to lead any evidence in her defence, therefore, DE was closed and the matter was adjourned for final arguments. 20. Final arguments were thereafter heard on behalf of state as well as the accused.
texts.arguments: 21. In the course of final argument, it was argued by the defence counsel that nothing incriminating has been found as per the report of FSL, in the sample which was collected in the presence of the principal and the police official. Further, it was claimed that as per the testimony of PW2 who was the principal the food was first used to be tested by the committee before it was given to the students. It was also contended by the defence that Principal herself was not aware as to who was the head of the said committee and then upon suggestion put to her, affirmed the she herself was the head or anyone appointed by her. Further, it has also come in her evidence that on the fateful day also, the food was tested and nothing was found and therefore, if later on the lizard was found in the meal it was for the school to explain. The counsel also contended that Principal even could not tell the name of the teacher who received the meal on the day of the incident. Thus, brushing away any liability on her part. It was also pointed by the defence counsel that after the incident the same NGO continued to State Vs. Archana Gupta FIR No.384/2011, PS Uttam Nagar, Page No. 11 of 17 Judgment dated 25.08.2022 supply the mid-day meal. Lastly, it was averred that the committee which received the food and distributed it among the students were liable for the incident and not the accused. 22. Per-contra, it was the arguments of the Ld. APP for the state that from all the materials available on record to convict the accused as PW5 Reeva Sood who was the director of the trust has clearly testified that accused was responsible for transporting the meal to the concerned school. Furthermore, the FSL report are not conclusive proof. 25. The ingredients of offence U/s 336/337 IPC are that the impugned act must of rash and negligence so as to endanger human life or personal safety and hurt must have been caused to some persons by such rash or negligent act. State vs . Archana Gupta on 25 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171946125/ 6 26. Also, in Mohan Shayam vs. The State (NCT of Delhi) dated 25.05.2012, wherein on the similar facts, it was held by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi that "In order to prove the act of negligence and rashness, it must be shown that the act was done without proper State Vs. Archana Gupta FIR No.384/2011, PS Uttam Nagar, Page No. 12 of 17 Judgment dated 25.08.2022 record to its consequences and without any precautions taken for ensuring the safety of others". 27. Criminal negligence has also been discussed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the landmark judgment of S.N. Hussain vs. State of Andhra Pradesh, AIR 1972, SC 685 as under: "Criminal negligence on the other hand, is the gross and culpable neglect or failure to exercise that reasonable proper care and precaution to guard against injuries either to the public generally or to an individual particular, which, having regard to all the circumstance out of which the charge has arisen it was the imperative duty of the accused person to have adopted. Culpable negligence lies in the failure to exercise reasonable and proper care and the extent of reasonableness will always depend upon the circumstances of each case". 28. State Vs. Archana Gupta FIR No.384/2011, PS Uttam Nagar, Page No. 14 of 17 Judgment dated 25.08.2022 State vs . Archana Gupta on 25 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171946125/ 7 30. Hence, if the food was checked when State Vs. Archana Gupta FIR No.384/2011, PS Uttam Nagar, Page No. 15 of 17 Judgment dated 25.08.2022 it was so received in the school as it is reflected from the statement of the PW2 i.e., the principal of the school, then how the lizard came to be found in the food? 34. Thus, in the attendance of so many ambiguities and flaws, the conviction of the accused cannot be justified as it is the most sacrosanct principle of criminal justice that any offence should be proved beyond reasonable doubts against the accused before he/she can be held liable i.e., the evidences should be proved in such a compact manner that it should be impervious to any let-out clause for State Vs. Archana Gupta FIR No.384/2011, PS Uttam Nagar, Page No. 16 of 17 Judgment dated 25.08.2022 the accused.
